Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.

slides.say: A bakery sends twice as many loaves to supermarkets as to cafés. One half of the supermarket loaves and one fifth of the café loaves are whole-wheat. What fraction of all the loaves is whole-wheat?
There are two groups of loaves, and each group has a different fraction of whole-wheat. We'll solve it two ways, by plugging in numbers, and then with an estimate.

We could write the cafés as x and the supermarkets as two x, and build an equation. But no amounts are given, only fractions, so plugging in numbers is more comfortable. Let's try one loaf for the cafés and two for the supermarkets. That's twice as many, good.
Half of the supermarket loaves are whole-wheat. Half of two is one, fine. A fifth of the café loaves. A fifth of one loaf? That's no good, we can't have part of a loaf.

No problem. We chose the numbers, so we may change them. The café total must be divisible by five, so a fifth is whole. The smallest possible total is five. So five café loaves, and twice that, ten supermarket loaves.
A fifth of five is one whole-wheat loaf. Half of ten is five whole-wheat loaves. Together, one plus five is six whole-wheat loaves. All the loaves are five plus ten, fifteen loaves.
at: A fifth of five is one

slides.say: So that's six out of fifteen. Six fifteenths reduces by three to two fifths. Choice number one is our answer.
at: Choice number one is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's estimate. We start again from the givens. If both groups were half whole-wheat, then all the loaves together would be half whole-wheat. But the café group is only a fifth, less than a half. So all together it's less than a half.
A half itself, choice number two, is out. And seven tenths is more than a half, so choice number three is out too.
at: so choice number three is out

slides.say: Now the other end. If both groups were a fifth whole-wheat, all together would be a fifth. But the supermarket group is a half, more than a fifth. So all together it's more than a fifth. One sixth is less than a fifth, so choice number four is out.
at: If both groups were a fifth
so choice number four is out

slides.say: Only two fifths is between a fifth and a half. This is worth remembering. When two groups are mixed, the fraction of the whole mix always lands between the fractions of the two groups. Choice number one is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: between a fifth and a half
Choice number one is our answer
